hook_candidates.spoken: Which plant has the biggest single flower in the world?
hook_candidates.visual: question mark over the record door

hook_candidates.spoken: The world's biggest single flower stinks of rotting meat.
Name the titan arum as the biggest single flower at quiz night and you lose the point.
I lie down inside the giant flower to compare. Watch.

sources.title: Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University, FAQ titan arum: Rafflesia arnoldii, native to the tropical rain forests of southeast Asia including Sumatra and Borneo, produces the world's largest single flower at about a meter in width; the titan arum's flowers are tiny, it is the world's largest unbranched inflorescence and can grow 8 to 10 feet (3 meters) in height
sources.label: Harvard Arboretum

sources.title: Oxford Botanic Garden, Chasing plants: in search of Rafflesia: Rafflesia arnoldii from the rainforests of Indonesian Sumatra produces the largest single flower in the world, over a metre across; Rafflesia has no roots, leaves or stems, lives inside a tropical vine and appears only to bloom; the flowers emit a stench of rotting meat that attracts flies, which cross pollinate the flowers
sources.label: Oxford Botanic Garden

sources.title: University of Hawaii at Manoa, Rafflesia (G. Carr): the flowers of R. arnoldii, up to a meter across, are the largest of any angiosperm
sources.label: Univ. of Hawaii

layout.description: Plümo thought he was the finest flower in the garden. The record belongs to Rafflesia arnoldii from Sumatra: about a meter wide, no roots, leaves or stems, and it lures flies with a smell of rotting meat. The titan arum is taller, but it is a cluster of many tiny flowers.

beats.spoken: World's biggest single flower? Not me. It's the rafflesia, about a meter wide.
Wait. I thought I was the finest flower in the garden. But no, I'm not even a flower. The record belongs to the rafflesia. I was shocked. The rafflesia was not.
How does it live? In the rainforests of Sumatra. No roots, no leaves, no stems. It lives inside a tropical vine and only shows up to bloom. No hands, so I point with my leaf.
Closer. The flowers stink of rotting meat. That lures flies looking to lay eggs. Along the way, they pollinate the flowers. Sneaky trick. One sniff. Nose off.
And the titan arum? Up to three meters tall. But not a single flower: a cluster of many tiny flowers. The rafflesia is one single flower, about a meter wide. I'm zero flowers.
Remember: rafflesia has the world's biggest single flower. Right, my turn. Scanner on. Result: bloom unknown. I guess I'm a bud.
I'll just lie here for a bit. More Zonkfruit? Follow the channel. I'll get up in a minute.
